column3: Office CMBS delinquency breaks above 12.00% and HOLDS for 2 consecutive monthly prints
column10: Currently 11.57% (Jun), +4bps MoM, 43bps below trigger. Path Jan 12.34 -> Feb 11.4 -> Apr 11.69 -> May 11.53 -> Jun 11.57 = it has been RANGE-BOUND for 5 months, and it already printed above 12 in January and fell back. Sub-50% because the "holds 2 consecutive" clause is doing real work: a single spike is likelier than a sustained break, and mods/cures keep pulling it back.

column10: Currently 17.11% (Jun), +36bps MoM, 89bps from trigger. At the recent +36bps/mo pace that is ~2.5 months. Held below 50% because SS is the noisier series (large-loan returns to master servicer cause sharp reversals — May fell 91bps on exactly that), so the path is not monotonic. NOTE: this SUPERSEDES the design-spec's PRED-002 ("June office SS prints >17% vs May 16.75%"), which RESOLVED CORRECT at 17.11% before the workbook was built — logged as PRED-CREED-002a below.

column6: FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, Q2 2026 (~late Aug 2026)
column10: This is CREED's S3 trigger leg and the single most decision-relevant open item. Below 50% deliberately: the series has improved for SIX straight quarters, the Q1 print was still improving, and the counter-evidence this window is strong (ARI's book cleared at 99.7%; 8 of 11 CRE lenders held dividends; equity tape counter-signal strengthened). Betting against a 6-quarter trend needs more than a thesis.

column3: At least one ADDITIONAL public CRE mortgage REIT (beyond ARI, KREF, RC) announces a dividend cut, a strategic-alternatives review, a wind-down, or a whole-book sale
column10: Above 50% on structural grounds: 7 of 11 trade negative on 3mo, several below book, and ARI has now demonstrated that handing capital back is an acceptable outcome to a board — that is a template, and templates propagate. BXMT is the highest-probability single name (largest office-exposed, -17.1%/3mo, dividend still intact). Held at 60% not higher because 8 of 11 dividends are currently INTACT and the cohort is not under acute funding stress.

column3: The ARI plan of complete liquidation and dissolution receives stockholder approval (as opposed to being amended, terminated, or replaced by a merger/business combination)
column6: ARI definitive proxy + shareholder vote result (8-K Item 5.07)
column10: The board has already sold the $9B book, returned $3.75/sh, and stated dissolution is advisable — most of the wind-down is DONE, which makes approval the path of least resistance. Held at 70% not higher because the 8-K expressly reserves the board's right to "terminate, modify or amend" WITHOUT stockholder approval and to pursue a merger instead, and a $2.2B-total-asset REIT shell (BVPS $12.05 at the 4/24/26 close) is exactly the kind of vehicle that attracts an alternative proposal. [Basis corrected 7/27 on a SHADE reconciliation ask: the ~$1.3B figure previously used here is a Q1 (3/31) CASH line, pre-close, not post-sale total assets.]

column3: The MBA Q2 2026 CM/MF print shows the LIFE-INSURER holdings line rising by MORE than the Q1 pace of +$3.3B
column6: MBA Commercial/Multifamily Mortgage Debt Outstanding, Q2 2026 (~mid-Sept 2026)
column10: FALSIFIABLE TEST OF THE FAST-TO-SLOW MIGRATION THESIS (FLOW-CREED-08). The ARI->Athene ~$9B closed 2026-04-24, i.e. INSIDE Q2. If that book lands in the CM/MF life-insurer line it should swamp a +$3.3B run-rate. If the line does NOT move materially, then either the book sits outside this series (possible — classification of a whole-loan portfolio purchase by an annuity writer is not guaranteed to land in CM/MF) or CREED's read on where it landed is wrong. EITHER OUTCOME IS INFORMATIVE — pre-registered deliberately. -> SHADE.

column3: VNQ underperforms SPY by 10pp or more over any trailing 3-month window (the S8a trigger)
column10: Currently +2.04pp — REITs OUTPERFORMING, and the relative has moved AGAINST this trigger for three consecutive CREED sessions (-2.9pp 7/4 -> -1.6pp 7/20 -> +2.04pp 7/27). Requires a ~12pp swing. LOW deliberately: this is the counter-signal CREED is committed to honoring, and writing a low number here is the point — it holds the bear read accountable to the tape.

column3: KREF's legacy office exposure reaches BELOW 10% of portfolio by its Q4 2026 report (management's own stated target)
column10: Management guided to <10% by YE2026 from 18% at 6/30. That requires roughly halving the legacy office book in two quarters, in a market where office assets do not clear quickly at acceptable prices — the same illiquidity KREF is reserving against. Slightly below even: company targets on asset dispositions in illiquid markets slip more often than they land, and the fast paths (bulk sale at a discount) force realized losses management may prefer to defer.

column3: A monthly Trepp print shows matured-balloon / maturity defaults as the MAJORITY of new CMBS delinquencies for 2 consecutive months (the S2 trigger)
column6: Trepp monthly delinquency prints, new-delinquency composition
column10: The maturity-adjusted DQ at 9.53% (multi-year high) and the all-maturity-driven July mall transfers both point this direction, and 39% of 2026 hard maturities land in Q4 — so the mechanism is loading. Held at 30% because CREED does not currently receive the new-delinquency COMPOSITION split monthly (the top-5 detail is published, the full-population maturity-vs-term split is not consistently visible without Trepp primary). RESOLVABILITY RISK IS REAL: if the composition data stays unavailable this becomes STUCK, not wrong.

column3: Athene Holding's Q2 2026 mortgage-loan balance rises materially versus the 3/31/26 base of ~$93B (order of ~+10%, consistent with absorbing ARI's ~$9B), OR the acquired book is identifiable in Athene/Apollo Q2 disclosure under another classification
column6: Athene Holding Ltd 10-Q Q2 2026 'Mortgage loans' line (~Aug 2026); cross-check Apollo Global Management 10-Q Retirement Services segment
column10: SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION SURFACE for the fast-to-slow migration thesis, raised by SHADE 7/27 and registered here rather than left as prose. PRED-CREED-006 tests the MBA CM/MF life-insurer AGGREGATE; this row tests the ACQUIRER'S OWN BALANCE SHEET. The joint read is what carries the information: if BOTH move, FLOW-CREED-08 is confirmed at named-instance and aggregate level; if only Athene moves, the MBA series does not capture this channel and PRED-006 is a bad instrument, not a bad thesis; IF NEITHER MOVES, the deal did not land where CREED and SHADE both think it did and the migration read needs re-derivation. Timing note (SHADE, correct): the 4/24/26 close POSTDATES the 3/31/26 balance-sheet date every current Athene figure rests on, so Q2 is the FIRST place it can appear. Held at 70% not higher on CLASSIFICATION risk: Athene uses ACRA co-invest vehicles and a whole-loan portfolio can land in an unconsolidated sidecar, a securitization, or an 'investment funds' line rather than 'mortgage loans'. -> SHADE owns capital treatment/RBC/L3/ALM; CREED owns the CRE flow leg.
